item.title: REGISTER TODAY: Opportunity Rising Career Information Workshop
item.description:
The City of Columbus employs over 9,000 people in 600 different job titles with plans to fill hundreds of vacancies in 2023. Come learn about the application and selection process!

The City of Columbus and Ohio Means Jobs will be hosting a series of workshops that will cover the following topics:

  • The role of the Civil Service Commission
  • Benefits of working for the City of Columbus
  • How to apply for city employment
  • What to expect during the selection process
  • Creating an application profile


Workshops will be held at the following locations:

  • Hilltop Branch Library: Wednesday, Jan. 4, 2023, 4:00 PM – 7:00 PM

    9:00 AM – 11:00 AM
  • Driving Park Library: Monday, Jan. 9, 2023, 10:30 AM – 1:00 PM

    2:00 PM – 4:00 PM

item.title: Job Opportunities
item.description:
Job Opportunities

The Office of Diversity and Inclusion would like to share some high priority open positions within the City of Columbus. If you or anyone you know are looking for a new opportunity, please check out these positions below:

 

Mid-Ohio Regional Planning Commission (MORPC) 

  • Associate Planner
    • The Associate Planner is a professional position utilizing skills in planning, project management, communications, and critical thinking to lead and assist on multiple projects and programs. 
    • This position requires a bachelor's degree in City and Regional Planning, Geography, Public Policy, Transportation Planning, Urban Planning, or related field plus a minimum of two years of related experience. An advanced degree in the appropriate field of study is acceptable as a substitute for experience.
  • Executive Scheduler -$21.00/hr 
    • Under the supervision of the Senior Director of Government Affairs & Community Relations, the Executive Scheduler is responsible for support of the Executive Director, Senior Director of Government Affairs & Community Relations, and Membership Services Officer in a range of tasks, establishing and improving communication to better serve the interests of local governments, and building relationships with elected and appointed officials, the private business sector and community groups.
    • This position requires a working knowledge of the principles, practices, and techniques of urban transportation modeling and planning. The ideal candidate would possess experience using transportation modeling software and GIS.
  • Director of Data Analytics & Strategy- $105,000.00 - $112,000.00
    • The Mid-Ohio Regional Planning Commission (MORPC) is seeking a dynamic, innovative, and qualified Director to lead our Data & Geospatial Analysis team. 
    • The Data & Geospatial Analysis team manages MORPC’s internal data resources and provides data collection, analysis, and visualization support to the agency’s other departments in areas ranging from transportation planning to community development, sustainability, population analysis, and community engagement. It also initiates and leads community research projects.

For additional information on MORPC Careers click here.

COSI

  • Director of Donor Engagement & Events
    • The Director of Donor Engagement & Events is responsible for developing and implementing the fundraising strategy for signature events at COSI as well as developing and implementing the organization’s donor stewardship plan. This role will work closely with internal and external stakeholders to generate and sustain philanthropic support for COSI.
    • Bachelor’s degree and 5+ years of fundraising, sales, or marketing experience. Experience soliciting and closing gifts or sales.
  • Manager of Local External Affairs and Public Policy
    • This position will develop key partnerships in the public arena with a focus toward ensuring that partnerships are on track and raise public funds to support and grow COSI’s key initiatives and organizational goals. 
    • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field required. Minimum of 2 years of demonstrated experience in external affairs and building successful partnerships in a business, nonprofit, museum, government agency, NGO, or equivalent with strategic engagement of community relevance and appeal, especially in the local public arena.
  • Director of External Affairs
    • This position supports the engagement with federal government agencies, community partners, and external groups, and will also oversee a team supporting state and local affairs, to ensure that partnerships are on track, raising public funds to support and grow COSI’s key initiatives and organizational goals. 
    • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field required. Master’s degree preferred. Minimum of 4 years of demonstrated experience in external affairs and building successful partnerships in a business, nonprofit, museum, government agency, NGO, or equivalent with strategic engagement of community relevance and appeal. Management experience also preferred.

For more information on COSI careers click here. 

 

We appreciate your partnership.

item.title: Job Opportunities
item.description:
Job Opportunities

The Office of Diversity and Inclusion would like to share some high priority open positions within the City of Columbus. If you or anyone you know are looking for a new opportunity, please check out these positions below:

Office of the Mayor

  • Director of Digital Communications- $31.00 to $46.48/hour
    • The successful candidate will be responsible for developing and implementing social media strategies and campaigns and other digital efforts for the Mayor and City of Columbus. The position demands the ability to develop strategies and campaigns and produce content in a professional and timely manner in a fast-paced environment. Work experience with current and emerging social media platforms and the ability to track analytics and how to incorporate them into campaigns are a must. Additionally, candidates should be organized and able to work as part of a team, collaborating closely with the marketing and graphic design manager.

To apply click here.

Mid-Ohio Regional Planning Commission (MORPC) 

  • Public Information Specialist - Depends on Qualifications
    • The Public Information Specialist supports the Executive Director, the Sr. Director of Communications & Engagement, senior executive team, and departments in formulating internal and external communications.
    • Write speeches and prepare talking points for Executive Director.
      Prepares and disseminates media releases, talking points, fact sheets, articles; respond to media inquiries, develop, and proactively pitch story ideas.
  • Associate or Senior Level- Planner, Modeler, Engineer -$60,000.00 - $80,000.00 
    • The Associate or Senior Planner/Engineer/Modeler is a professional position that requires the practice of basic engineering, planning, and research skills in transportation travel demand modeling. The position will support or manage the day-to-day projects.
    • This position requires a working knowledge of the principles, practices, and techniques of urban transportation modeling and planning. The ideal candidate would possess experience using transportation modeling software and GIS.

YWCA Columbus

  • Justice, Equity & Belonging Program Manager- $55,000.00-$60,000.00
    • The Justice, Equity & Belonging Program Manager is responsible for co-developing and facilitating activities related to educating the community about justice, equity, and belonging. Responsible for the design and implementation of trainings on racial equity, belonging, restorative practices, anti-racism and other social justice concepts; and promoting partnerships that support the organization’s mission and values.

To apply email resumes to Caroline Woliver at cwoliver@ywcacolumbus.org

COSI

  • Director of Youth STEM Programs
    • This role will have responsibility for planning, content development, establishment of partnerships, and implementation of THE PLATFORM program - a new signature education initiative for COSI. The Director of Youth STEM Programs will leverage their expertise in education, youth intervention, advocacy and mentor development to help program participants (students) achieve their academic goals and objectives.
  • Senior Director of Technology Systems
    • This position will support all aspects of the institution’s business, including its retail, e-commerce, and building systems. This role collaborates with departments as a strategic partner to provide in-depth technical expertise in support of decisions related to technology integration. This position is responsible for researching new technologies, driving implementation of best practices for optimizing infrastructure, and improving information system performance and security.
  • Director of Exhibit Experiences
    • Support COSI’s mission by ensuring excellence in the development and production of educational, attractive and functional guest experiences. Provide conceptual and tactical direction as well as project management for the research, design, development, production, and fabrication of new experiences; deliver upon the COSI’s mission, vision, and strategic goals including the identification and development of COSI onsite experiences; support the ongoing enhancement of the permanent exhibition base as well as traveling exhibitions.

We appreciate your partnership.

Job Opportunities

The Office of Diversity and Inclusion would like to share some high priority open positions within the City of Columbus and our external partners. If you or anyone you know are looking for a new opportunity, please check out these positions below:

 

The Central Ohio Area Agency on Aging

Aging Programs Administer- Are you looking for the next step in your career? Would you like the opportunity to lead an amazing agency whose mission is to assist the aging population and those with disabilities of all ages remain safe and healthy in their homes?

If so, then an Aging Programs Administrator position at The Central Ohio Area Agency on Aging (COAAA) is the right position for you!

Our agency is looking for you if your skills, knowledge and abilities include:

  • Program Planning & Evaluation
  • Knowledge of Public Policies Related to Older Adults & Individuals with Disabilities
  • Supervisory & Training Experience
  • Knowledge of Local & Community Resources
  • Preparing Documents, Manuals, Correspondence & Technical & Comprehensive Reports
  • Knowledge of Methods Used in Current Business Operations
  • Planning, Coordinating & Evaluating Major Work Sections or Program Activities
  • Public Speaking
  • Reviewing, Analyzing & Evaluating Data & Making Necessary Recommendations

The Aging Programs Administrator job duties would include:

  • Leading strategic planning activities and assuring goal achievement by the COAAA Team
  • Assuring quality improvement programs are in place for the organization
  • Developing policies and procedures for COAAA
  • Public and private fund-raising activities 
  • Meeting with COAAA Advisory Council to formulate plans and resolves problems
  • Assuring financial accountability
  • Directing the personnel administration, the operations of service programs and the acquirement of service providers
  • Developing and maintaining key relationships with various community entities

If interested please apply at https://www.governmentjobs.com/careers/columbusoh. All applications must be submitted by no later than Monday, February 28, 2022

 

We appreciate your partnership.

COSI 

Director of Donor Engagement & Events - is responsible for developing and implementing the fundraising strategy for signature events at COSI, as well as concepting and overseeing the implementation of cultivation-focused and donor stewardship events. This position will work to grow COSI signature events and donor engagement in this area, develop and enhance relationships with event donors and volunteer leaders, deliver exceptional customer service, and generate new ideas and strategies to maintain and enhance a dynamic, compelling fundraising program. The Director of Donor Engagement & Events will maintain an active portfolio of donors and prospects, and will work closely with internal and external stakeholders to generate and sustain philanthropic support for COSI.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree and 5+ years of fundraising, sales, event, or marketing experience

Senior Manager of Corporate Giving -  is responsible for raising vital philanthropic support for COSI through intentional relationship management of corporate prospects and donors, and engagement with fundraising strategy for programs and initiatives that appeal to businesses and corporations. This position will be required to solicit support from a portfolio of 100-125 businesses and corporations in order to achieve an assigned annual contributed revenue goal. The ideal candidate will be able to identify and qualify prospects, thoughtfully cultivate managed relationships, undertake strategic solicitations and/or prepare customized proposals, and provide excellent stewardship to assigned donors.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree and 3+ years of progressive experience in a fundraising environment

  • Project management experience and the ability to work efficiently in a collaborative setting

  • Social Worker and Registered Nurse Case Managers – Are you looking for a job that gives you a sense of fulfillment or perhaps an employer whose mission and values align with your own? Would you like to help the aging population and those with disabilities of all ages remain safe and healthy in their homes? If so, then a Case Manager position at The Central Ohio Area Agency on Aging (COAAA) is the right position for you! Our fast-paced programs are looking for you if your skills include: Problem-Solving & Decision-Making, Conflict Resolution, Relationship Building, Organizational & Time Management, Critical Thinking, and Communication & Interpersonal. As a Case Manager you would be expected to:
    • Fulfill the needs and the requirements of your respected program
    • Assess an individual’s needs for care
    • Create appropriate care plans
    • Complete home visits
    • Collaborate with clients and other team members
    • Coordinate services of care with outside entities/agencies
    • Learn various computer systems
    • Adapt to a changing work environment

Minimum qualifications: Possession of a valid State of Ohio license as a Social Worker and Possession of a valid Motor Vehicle operator’s license.
Preferred Qualifications: One year of case management experience, One year of completing home-visits experience, One year of connecting individuals to resources and services, Experience working with Microsoft Excel, A Bachelor’s degree or higher

item.title: MORPC Regional Mobility Plan
item.description:
Opportunity for you to share your VOICE

The Mid-Ohio Regional Planning Commission (MORPC) is working with nine Central Ohio counties to develop a transit coordinated plan for the ODOT Human Service Transportation Coordination Region 6 – the Regional Mobility Plan.

The Regional Mobility Plan will identify local transportation needs of people with disabilities, older adults, and those with low incomes. It will help to provide strategies for meeting those needs and prioritize transportation services regarding projects for funding and implementation.

The draft version of the plan is now available for review at  https://www.morpc.org/program-service/regional-mobility-plan/.  Comments can be submitted by email to apetrella@morpc.org or in writing to MORPC, 111 Liberty Street - Suite 100, Columbus, Ohio 43215, Attn: Lexi Petrella, by 5 p.m. on Sunday, Dec. 19, 2021.

MORPC will also host two upcoming virtual public meetings. Members of the public are encouraged to attend one of the two online presentations that will include a question and comment period.

item.title: Great Things are Happening in Columbus
item.description:
Great Things are Happening in Columbus

The Office of Diversity and Inclusion knows how important it is for everyone to be able to be their "True Selves" wherever they work, go to school or even live.  We are very excited to share a few things that our own City Councilmember, Priscilla Tyson and Shayla Favor have been working on to ensure that this is possible for Columbus.

Fighting Implicit Bias Relating to Natural Hair - Passed in Columbus, Ohio 

Councilmember Priscilla Tyson introduced a resolution to express support for the CROWN ACT (Creating a Respectful and Open World for Natural Hair) to protect Black Americans from race-based hair discrimination. The resolution was adopted on Monday, July 27, 2020.

The CROWN Act was created in 2019 to ensure protection against discrimination based on  race-based hairstyles by extending statutory protection to hair texture and protective styles such as braids, locs, twists, and knots in the workplace and public schools.

“These issues don’t stop in the adult and professional world,” Councilmember Shayla Favor said, who co-sponsored the resolution.

Hair discrimination remains a source of racial injustice with serious economic consequences for Black people. The CROWN Act corrects these racial injustices by making hair discrimination illegal.

To learn more about the CROWN Act, click here.

Commission on Black Girls Rolls Out Report

After two years of work, countless hours of public testimony, a survey focusing on Black Girls ages 11-22, and listening sessions, the Commission on Black Girls released the report outlining its findings and next steps to ensure Black girls in Columbus have equal access to opportunities for success.

"We took this journey to address the racial inequities that Black women experience in our community, said Councilmember Priscilla Tyson, founder of the Commission. "We want to change the life trajectory of Black women; therefore, it was necessary to begin with the early stages of development in Black girls' lives to create opportunities to improve their futures."

On July 16, 2018, Columbus City Council adopted resolution number 0208X-2018 to create the Commission on Black Girls. The Commission was charged with studying the quality of life of Black girls (ages 11-22 years old) in Columbus and Central Ohio. Further, the Commission was established to develop and implement recommendations to ensure opportunities, prosperous futures, and the attainment of a high quality of life is realized for all Black girls.

Dr. Frederic Bertley President and CEO of COSI and Frances C. Frazier of Rise Sister Rise serve as co-chairs for the Commission.

"It is an honor to support and co-chair, with Ms. Fran Frazier and the 24 other Commissioners, Councilmember Tyson's Commission on Black Girls," said Frederic Bertley, President and CEO, COSI Co-Chair, Commission on Black Girls. "This work and approach of examining the real-time status and condition of Black girls is not only precedent setting, but the Commission's process and product represents a necessary blueprint for urban cities across this country."

Researchers developed a survey that engaged more than 400 young girls and convened focus groups to assess the perspective of girls on their quality of life. The researchers focused on three quality of life indicators: economics, academics, and emotional health and well-being. Information was also compiled from listening sessions. These sessions allowed commissioners to hear from service providers, parents, caregivers, and girls between the ages of 11-22.

"The outcome of this important work is a series of recommendations that can and should be acted on to address important issues related to Black Girls, whose condition - mental health, physical health, education and economic agility and stability is indeed relevant to all Americans," Bertley continued. "I commend Councilmember Tyson on having the courage and fortitude to take on this bold but necessary initiative. Black girls in Columbus will be better for it. Columbus, Ohio, and the nation will be better for it."

In addition, The Commission hosted monthly meetings where they heard presentations from subject matter experts on topics such as physical health, behavioral health, education, juvenile justice, child welfare, social media, programs for Black girls and more.

Information received through the research and fact-finding efforts were used to inform the next steps. There is one overarching recommendation, three strategies and eighteen recommendations.
 
OVERARCHING RECOMMENDATION

The Commission on Black Girls will evolve from its current two-year temporary status into a permanent entity. The Commission will focus on engaging the community to implement the strategies and recommendations proposed in this report. The input collected and presented in this report will serve as the basis of launching the establishment of the permanent Commission as a data-driven center of excellence to positively transform the quality of life outcomes for Black girls in Columbus and Central Ohio.

  • Strategy #1: Create an environment that is free of racism that impairs the ability of Black girls to see themselves and be seen in a manner that fosters their ability to develop and maintain positive quality of life perspectives to the same extent as their non-Black peers.
  • Strategy #2: Create and strengthen holistic, systemic approaches to address and disrupt pervasive cycles of education, health, and economic, societal inequities that adversely impact the progress of Black girls toward their individual quality of life goals.
  • Strategy #3: Advocate for resources and initiatives to enhance the successful quality of life pathways for Black girls.

Many of the recommendations address: education, mentoring and leadership, healthcare, safety, racism and bias training, health and well-being, economics, issues experienced by LGBTQ+ youth and families and youth in the child welfare system.

“The work of the Commission on Black Girls, led by Councilmember Tyson, is a testament to the important work ahead to fight racism and sexism,” said Council President Shannon G. Hardin. “I look forward to supporting this effort as we work to level barriers to opportunity with our black girls.”

To view the report visit https://www.columbus.gov/cobgreport/

item.title: I can’t breathe
item.description:
I can’t breathe.

These words translate generations of fear, anger, despair, powerlessness, pressure and exhaustion. As a member of Mayor Ginther’s leadership team and a proud mother of African-American children, I know that it is paramount that we treat racism like the systemic disease it is and come together as a city to mobilize and dialogue and to actively work on lifting and empowering. We need to support all of the residents of Columbus – not just those with the most political clout or the most money. We must center race in our work and policy decision making, data has shown us over and over again that communities of color are most disproportionately and adversely affected by disease as we are seeing with COVID-19. Communities of color are most affected by police brutality, access to fair and affordable housing, health care and other aspects of disparities.

Mayor Ginther did not start working on addressing these issues seven days ago or even at his State of the City address in February. He began on day one by creating the Office of Diversity and Inclusion. He called for the first disparity study in Columbus since 1993. He signed an executive order to accelerate the recommendations of the disparity study just weeks ago.

Addressing racism and disparity must be a multi-pronged approach from addressing police reform to making sure all residents have the opportunity to build wealth.

The Office of Diversity and Inclusion continues to work with Mayor Ginther and the people of Columbus to flatten the racism curve while enabling all of us to work together to enable economic equality -- and to simply breathe without fear.

Beverly Stallings-Johnson, PhD
Chief Diversity Officer

item.title: Message from Mayor Ginther
item.description:
I understand why some residents are angry.  I'm angry, too.  Angry at the injustices perpetrated on our black and brown brothers and sisters.  Angry at the racism that persists in our country year after year.

We know that racism exists in our city, in our neighborhoods, in the workplace and in the Columbus Division of Police.  Chief Quinlan has been making solid steps toward implementing plans to flush out racism and to eliminate it from the ranks.  He is working to improve community police relations.

We need to hire more people of color to be police officers to reflect the diversity of our beautiful city, and we are working hard to do that. We have started a cadet program to work as a pipeline to recruit more women and men of color to serve.  Our last police recruit classes have shown greater diversity than in the last decade.

This isn't enough.  We can do more and we will.  Chief Quinlan is forming a chief's council to hear directly from residents.  He formed the Police and Community Together Team (PACT) to address human trafficking with the community.  He has put in place officer wellness checks before incidents happen and has eliminated officers’ ability to use accrued leave to pay off suspensions.

Real change is a community effort.  And it is hard. It takes every one of us to make change happen.  And yes, it takes protests to show anger and frustration.

But protests must remain peaceful.  Last night, a few people used the opportunity of the protest to vandalize the Statehouse, the Ohio Theatre and other businesses downtown.  That accomplishes nothing and will not be tolerated.  Nor will throwing objects at the police.

Neighbors, this is our city.  It is what we make it.  Let's use our frustration not to tear down and destroy but to lift up and make change.
